 Taylor Swift and Dolly Parton recorded music at a Tennessee retreat built in 1998; after more than 65 gold and platinum albums were made there, the 10-acre studio estate is now listed for $19.5 million 
 TOI Real Estate Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Nov 18, 2026, 12:10 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Tennessee studio estate where Taylor Swift and Dolly Parton recorded lists for $19.5 millionPhoto credit (L-R): Wikipedia, ANI, and zillow.com A Tennessee retreat where Taylor Swift and Dolly Parton have recorded music is now on the market for $19.5 million. Dark Horse Estate in Franklin, built in 1998 on just over 10 acres, has hosted more than 65 gold and platinum albums and is being offered as a rare combination of private residence, working studio, and entertainment compound, according to Realtor.com. The 23,138 square foot property includes Dark Horse Manor, Dark Horse Recording, The Cottage, The Bungalow Apartment, and The Party Barn. Its listing presents it as a place where artists can escape, focus, and create, with multiple studios, guest quarters, gathering spaces, and room for entertaining. 
 A studio with a serious track record
 Dark Horse Recording has become one of the more notable creative spaces in the Nashville area. The estate has been used by artists including Taylor Swift , Dolly Parton , Keith Urban, Reba McEntire, Amy Grant, Peter Frampton, Florida Georgia Line, and Darius Rucker. More than 65 gold and platinum albums have been recorded there, according to the listing. That history gives the property a cultural identity that goes beyond its square footage or acreage. The studio is not just a feature of the home. It is a central part of the estate’s identity, making the listing appealing to buyers who want a live and work property with an established creative pedigree. What the estate contains
 Dark Horse Manor is the main residence and offers facilities for recording music. The Cottage and The Bungalow Apartment offer private guest accommodations, allowing visiting artists or collaborators to stay on site. The Party Barn is another layer of appeal to the property. It gives the estate a place to hold gatherings, events or creative sessions beyond the studio itself. The compound also includes a three car garage, covered walkways, a sky bridge, and a game room. These details suggest that the property was designed not only for recording but for a lifestyle built around privacy, hospitality, and creative work, as per the report. Dark Horse Estate in FranklinPhoto credit: zillow.com Outdoor space built for inspiration
 The estate sits on 10.01 acres, offering a level of privacy that is hard to find close to Nashville. The grounds are intended as a retreat, with natural surroundings and space to get away from the pace of the city. More than 3,000 square feet of covered porches and walkways overlook the property. These outdoor areas are intended for entertaining and relaxation, but they also give the estate a calm atmosphere that can support creative work. The combination of indoor studios and outdoor space makes the property more than a typical luxury listing. It is built for people who want to live, work, host guests, and create in one place. 
 Why the price is $19.5 million
 The $19.5 million asking price reflects more than the size of the home. It reflects the land, the scale of the compound, the recording facilities, and the estate’s history with major artists. The property has already drawn attention, reaching the top of Realtor.com’s weekly most popular homes list. That visibility may help attract buyers who understand the value of a turnkey creative estate. For a buyer in the music industry, the estate offers an immediate opportunity to continue operating a studio with a proven track record. For a private buyer, it offers a rare chance to own a large, secluded property with built in entertainment and guest space. Join conversation

 A property with a story
 Dark Horse Estate is not being marketed as just another luxury home. It is being sold as a piece of Nashville’s creative history, with a list of artists whose work has passed through its studios. The fact that Taylor Swift and Dolly Parton are among the names associated with the property gives it a level of recognition that most estates cannot match. That history may matter as much to buyers as the physical features of the home. As the listing moves forward, the question is whether the next owner will preserve the estate’s role as a working studio or reshape it into a private residence. Either way, the property enters the market with a story that few homes can claim.
